title: The Craft of Controlled Surgery
mathematical_role: Represent recognition of a local S² × I neck, cutting on spherical cross-sections, removal, cap attachment, and the event ledger as one coherent staged composition.
learning_objective: Remember surgery as a theorem-governed geometric transaction with explicit topology bookkeeping, not arbitrary planar cut-and-paste.
literal_semantics: The teaching sequence is recognize neck → cut/remove → attach cap models and continue.
The local neck type is explicitly labelled S² × I.
The event ledger asks what is cut, what survives, and what reverse equation is recorded.
nonliteral_semantics: The sculptural forms are perspective schematics, not literal metric three-manifolds.
Dashed cross-sections are pictorial stand-ins for cutting two-spheres.
Cap shapes are teaching models, not numerically constructed surgery caps.
Displayed size and shape are not surgery scales.

accessibility.alt_text: A sculptural three-stage S2-by-I neck sequence moves from recognition through controlled cutting and removal to capped components; an event ledger records the topology transaction.
accessibility.long_description: Three large geometric stages dominate the plate: a marked S2 by I neck, two projected cutting spheres with the middle region removed, and capped components. An event-ledger panel lists the bookkeeping needed to preserve history.
